name: Jabin and Sisera
charge: Mightily oppressing Israel twenty years with nine hundred chariots of iron
summary: Jabin reigned in Hazor and Sisera commanded his host, and for twenty years they mightily oppressed the children of Israel. Deborah sent for Barak, the Lord discomfited the chariots at Kishon, and Sisera died in a tent with a nail through his temples.
offense: After Ehud died, Israel again did evil, and the Lord sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan. Sisera, his captain, commanded nine hundred chariots of iron and oppressed Israel mightily for twenty years (Judges 4:1-3). The iron chariots explain the terror of the servitude; they do not explain away the Lord's government of it. Israel had returned to sin after rest, and the enemy was again given the upper hand. The song describes what oppression did to ordinary life. Highways lay unoccupied, travellers used byways, and village life ceased until Deborah arose (Judges 5:6-7). It then names the departure beneath the disorder: Israel chose new gods, and war was in the gates (Judges 5:8). Their worship and their public condition were not separate matters. The people who would not be ruled by the Lord found themselves ruled by the force of Canaan.
judgment: The Lord appointed the place of the confrontation. Deborah told Barak to draw ten thousand men toward Mount Tabor; the Lord would draw Sisera, his chariots, and his multitude to the river Kishon and deliver him into Barak's hand (Judges 4:6-7). The enemy's gathering was therefore not an interruption of the promise. It brought the host to the place where the promise would be fulfilled. At Deborah's word Barak descended, and the Lord discomfited Sisera's army. The captain abandoned his chariot and fled on foot, while Barak pursued the host until none remained (Judges 4:14-16). Judges 5:20-21 names the stars fighting and Kishon sweeping the enemy away. Deuteronomy 20:1 had forbidden Israel to fear horses, chariots, and a greater people when the Lord was with them. What appeared to establish Sisera's superiority could not preserve him against that word. Sisera reached Jael's tent, but did not reach safety. She killed him there, fulfilling Deborah's declaration that the honour of taking him would go to a woman (Judges 4:9, 17-22). Jabin's destruction followed as Israel's hand grew stronger against him (Judges 4:23-24). The song ends with Sisera's household expecting spoil while the captain never returns, and with forty years of rest for Israel (Judges 5:28-31). The oppressor's expectation and the Lord's judgment were opposite things.

verses.text: And the children of Israel again did evil in the sight of the Lord, when Ehud was dead.
And the Lord sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, that reigned in Hazor; the captain of whose host was Sisera, which dwelt in Harosheth of the Gentiles.
And the children of Israel cried unto the Lord: for he had nine hundred chariots of iron; and twenty years he mightily oppressed the children of Israel.
And they shewed Sisera that Barak the son of Abinoam was gone up to mount Tabor.
And Sisera gathered together all his chariots, even nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the people that were with him, from Harosheth of the Gentiles unto the river of Kishon.

And Deborah said unto Barak, Up; for this is the day in which the Lord hath delivered Sisera into thine hand: is not the Lord gone out before thee? So Barak went down from mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.
And the Lord discomfited Sisera, and all his chariots, and all his host, with the edge of the sword before Barak; so that Sisera lighted down off his chariot, and fled away on his feet.
But Barak pursued after the chariots, and after the host, unto Harosheth of the Gentiles: and all the host of Sisera fell upon the edge of the sword; and there was not a man left.
Howbeit Sisera fled away on his feet to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite: for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
And Jael went out to meet Sisera, and said unto him, Turn in, my lord, turn in to me; fear not. And when he had turned in unto her into the tent, she covered him with a mantle.
And he said unto her, Give me, I pray thee, a little water to drink; for I am thirsty. And she opened a bottle of milk, and gave him drink, and covered him.
Again he said unto her, Stand in the door of the tent, and it shall be, when any man doth come and enquire of thee, and say, Is there any man here? that thou shalt say, No.

Then Jael Heber’s wife took a nail of the tent, and took an hammer in her hand, and went softly unto him, and smote the nail into his temples, and fastened it into the ground: for he was fast asleep and weary. So he died.

And, behold, as Barak pursued Sisera, Jael came out to meet him, and said unto him, Come, and I will shew thee the man whom thou seekest. And when he came into her tent, behold, Sisera lay dead, and the nail was in his temples.
So God subdued on that day Jabin the king of Canaan before the children of Israel.
And the hand of the children of Israel prospered, and prevailed against Jabin the king of Canaan, until they had destroyed Jabin king of Canaan.
The kings came and fought, then fought the kings of Canaan in Taanach by the waters of Megiddo; they took no gain of money.
They fought from heaven; the stars in their courses fought against Sisera.
The river of Kishon swept them away, that ancient river, the river Kishon. O my soul, thou hast trodden down strength.
Then were the horsehoofs broken by the means of the pransings, the pransings of their mighty ones.
Blessed above women shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be, blessed shall she be above women in the tent.
He asked water, and she gave him milk; she brought forth butter in a lordly dish.
She put her hand to the nail, and her right hand to the workmen’s hammer; and with the hammer she smote Sisera, she smote off his head, when she had pierced and stricken through his temples.
At her feet he bowed, he fell, he lay down: at her feet he bowed, he fell: where he bowed, there he fell down dead.
The mother of Sisera looked out at a window, and cried through the lattice, Why is his chariot so long in coming? why tarry the wheels of his chariots?
Her wise ladies answered her, yea, she returned answer to herself,

Have they not sped? have they not divided the prey; to every man a damsel or two; to Sisera a prey of divers colours, a prey of divers colours of needlework, of divers colours of needlework on both sides, meet for the necks of them that take the spoil?
So let all thine enemies perish, O Lord: but let them that love him be as the sun when he goeth forth in his might. And the land had rest forty years.
Do unto them as unto the Midianites; as to Sisera, as to Jabin, at the brook of Kison:
Which perished at En–dor: they became as dung for the earth.

entries.commentary: When Ehud was dead, the children of Israel again did evil, and the Most High sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, that reigned in Hazor, whose captain was Sisera, which dwelt in Harosheth of the Gentiles. Sisera had nine hundred chariots of iron, and twenty years he mightily oppressed the children of Israel, and they cried unto the Most High.

Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, judged Israel at that time, dwelling under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in mount Ephraim, and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment. She calls Barak the son of Abinoam and gives him the commandment of the Most High: draw toward mount Tabor with ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun, and I will draw unto thee Sisera with his chariots and his multitude to the river Kishon, and deliver him into thine hand. Barak answers, if thou wilt go with me, then I will go, but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go. Deborah agrees to go, but tells him the journey shall not be for his honour, for the Most High shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman.

Barak calls Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh and goes up with ten thousand men at his feet, and Deborah goes up with him. Heber the Kenite, of the children of Hobab the father in law of Moses, had severed himself from the Kenites and pitched his tent by Kedesh. Sisera gathers all nine hundred chariots of iron unto the river of Kishon, and Deborah says unto Barak, up, for this is the day in which the Lord hath delivered Sisera into thine hand; is not the Lord gone out before thee? The Most High discomfits Sisera and all his chariots and all his host with the edge of the sword before Barak; Sisera lights down off his chariot and flees away on his feet, and all his host falls upon the edge of the sword; there was not a man left.

Sisera flees on foot to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber. Jael invites him in, covers him with a mantle, and gives him milk to drink when he asks for water. He tells her to stand in the door and say no man is there; then Jael takes a nail of the tent and a hammer in her hand, goes softly unto him as he sleeps fast and weary, and smites the nail into his temples and fastens it into the ground, and he dies. The word through Deborah stands: Sisera was sold into the hand of a woman. When Barak comes pursuing, Jael shows him Sisera lying dead with the nail in his temples. So God subdued that day Jabin the king of Canaan before the children of Israel, and their hand prospered and prevailed until they had destroyed him. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant)

Deborah and Barak sing praise to the Lord for the avenging of Israel, when the people willingly offered themselves. That is what the Most High wants from us: a willing heart in all that we do, in the keeping of the commandments, in the keeping of the feast days, and in the praise of him.
The Lord marching out of the field of Edom, the earth trembling, the heavens dropping, and the mountains melting from before the Lord God of Israel is future prophecy; this has not happened yet.

This passage is for all the closet feminists who think Deborah justifies women leading men. She did not lead men into any kind of war; she did not put on body armor and a breastplate, rise up on a horse, and lead the charge. She was the motivating factor to men that were shaky and fearful during that time, a mother in Israel, a guiding light. Verse 9 proves it: my heart is toward the governors of Israel, the leaders who offered themselves willingly among the people. Her heart was with the men who led; she was not ruling over them.

They that are delivered from the noise of archers in the places of drawing water shall rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord. That is where we are right now: in the places of drawing water, rehearsing the righteous acts of the Most High while the arrows are still being shot.

The song rehearses which tribes came out. Out of Ephraim, Benjamin, Machir, and Zebulun came governors and they that handle the pen of the writer, and the princes of Issachar were with Deborah and Barak in the valley. For the divisions of Reuben there were great thoughts and great searchings of heart: they were second-guessing themselves. Gilead abode beyond Jordan, Dan remained in ships, and Asher continued on the seashore; the song is getting on the tribes that stayed home. Zebulun and Naphtali were a people that jeoparded their lives unto the death in the high places of the field; those tribes are warriors.

The kings of Canaan fought by the waters of Megiddo and took no gain of money; they fought from heaven, and the stars in their courses fought against Sisera. Sisera is the general of the Canaanite host, not Syria; the river Kishon swept them away. The angel of the Lord said curse ye Meroz, curse ye bitterly the inhabitants thereof, because they came not to the help of the Lord against the mighty. Sitting out the battle of the Lord brings a curse.

Blessed above women in the tent shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be. Sisera asked water and she gave him milk; then she put her hand to the nail and her right hand to the workman's hammer, and where he bowed, there he fell down dead.

The mother of Sisera looked out at a window and cried, why is his chariot so long in coming? Her wise ladies answer her with imaginations of victory, that they are dividing the prey and the needlework spoil. She is looking for a son who is never coming home; he lay dead in Jael's tent. So let all thine enemies perish, O Lord: but let them that love him be as the sun when he goeth forth in his might. And the land had rest forty years.

The prayer opens asking the Most High to keep not silence, hold not His peace, and be not still, for His enemies make a tumult and they that hate Him have lifted up the head. This shows that God has enemies, and the chapter is about to name God's enemies right now. They have taken crafty counsel against His people, against us the Israelites, and consulted against His hidden ones, saying come let us cut them off from being a nation, that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance. This is why today, nowadays, we are separated from our history, according to [Jeremiah 17:5](/bible/jeremiah/17#v5). -

Here the enemies of God begin to be named. They have consulted together with one consent and are confederate against the Most High: the tabernacles of Edom and the Ishmaelites, of Moab and the Hagarenes. Gebal, and Ammon, and Amalek, the Philistines with the inhabitants of Tyre; Assur also is joined with them, and they have holpen the children of Lot.

David asks the Most High to do unto these enemies as unto the Midianites, as to Sisera and as to Jabin at the brook of Kison, who perished at Endor and became as dung for the earth. He asks that their nobles be made like Oreb and like Zeeb, all their princes as Zebah and as Zalmunna, who said let us take to ourselves the houses of God in possession.

He asks the Most High to make them like a wheel, as the stubble before the wind; as the fire burneth a wood and as the flame setteth the mountains on fire, so to persecute them with His tempest and make them afraid with His storm. The aim of the prayer is that their faces be filled with shame, that they may seek His name; that men may know that He whose name alone is JEHOVAH is the Most High over all the earth.
